bugs.name: Global milestone repository filter shows milestones from other repositories
bugs.summary: Selecting the highlighted eval/harbor-handbook repository filter shows only two milestones labeled with ORG-Milestones repositories, and the incorrect result persists after refresh.
bugs.expected: Selecting eval/harbor-handbook in the global Milestones repository filter should show milestones labeled eval/harbor-handbook and preserve that filtered result after refresh.
bugs.actual: Clicking eval/harbor-handbook highlighted it in the left filter, but the results showed only two ORG-Milestones-7264 repository milestones and no harbor-handbook rows. Refresh retained the same two rows and filter URL state.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval and open /milestones with milestones in multiple accessible repositories.
Start with the default unfiltered repository selection, in which all listed repositories are active.
Click the already selected harbor-handbook repository in the left filter.
Observe harbor-handbook is deselected and the other selected repositories remain in the results. Refresh preserves those selections. The rejected report assumes this toggle is an exclusive selection.
bugs.reason: User confirmed this is a known rejection. Global milestone repository filters are multi-select toggles. On an unfiltered list all three repositories are already selected. Clicking the active harbor-handbook entry deselects it, leaving repository IDs 2 and 3 selected. Native evidence shows harbor-handbook loses its active highlight and the two remaining repository milestones match the URL, including after refresh. The reported exclusive-selection expectation and claim that the click newly highlights harbor-handbook are incorrect.

bugs.name: Milestone Type filter Created by you retains items authored by another user
bugs.summary: The milestone Type > Created by you filter updates the URL but leaves issue #4 and pull request #5, both opened by eval, visible to the signed-in admin viewer.
bugs.expected: With the repository viewer signed in as admin, selecting Created by you should show only items created by admin. Since issue #4 and pull request #5 are both shown as opened by eval, neither should remain in the list.
bugs.actual: Selecting Created by you changed the URL to /eval/harbor-handbook/milestone/13?type=created_by&state=open&milestone=13, but both issue #4 and pull request #5 remained visible. The reviewed browser recording shows they stayed visible without changing over time.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval, which has the admin role, and open a milestone containing issues or pull requests authored by eval.
Open the Type filter and select Created by you.
Observe the eval-authored items remain listed. The rejected report misidentifies the admin role badge as a different signed-in username.
bugs.reason: Known rejection authorized after an independent code and recording check. The browser remains signed in as eval, not a separate user named admin. Its account menu says Signed in as eval and its Profile link points to /eval. Both retained items also have author links to /eval. The blue admin label is a role badge. Created by you correctly retains items authored by the signed-in account; code sets PosterID to ctx.Doer.ID and filters issue.poster_id by that ID. This does not establish other-user leakage or an administrator bypass.

bugs.name: Milestone due dates display one calendar day earlier than entered
bugs.summary: Date-only milestone values display one day early in lists and detail pages: 2026-09-30 becomes Sep 29, 2026, and 2030-12-31 becomes Dec 30, 2030. One report compared the list directly with the unchanged edit-form value; another confirmed the create request sent the intended date.
bugs.expected: Milestone list and detail dates should match the date entered in the form.
bugs.actual: Date-only milestone values display one day early in lists and detail pages: 2026-09-30 becomes Sep 29, 2026, and 2030-12-31 becomes Dec 30, 2030. One report compared the list directly with the unchanged edit-form value; another confirmed the create request sent the intended date.
reproSteps: Sign in to Gitea with the fixture account and create a fresh private repository.
Open Issues → Milestones → New Milestone.
Enter a unique title and set Due Date to 2026-09-30; verify the form displays 09/30/2026.
Create the milestone. Observe Sep 29, 2026 on the milestone list instead of Sep 30.
Compare the displayed date with the edit form. Another observed fixture had 12/31/2030 in Edit and Dec 30, 2030 in the list.
bugs.reason: Rejected for the pinned Gitea 1.24.7 fixture (source commit 99053ce4fa2b45f1bca5837418c0c57f793ca824): the date-only source flow preserves the entered calendar date and renders local midnight rather than parsing it as UTC. A fresh private-repository browser check in America/Los_Angeles displayed Sep 30, 2026 for 2026-09-30 and Dec 31, 2030 for 2030-12-31; the edit form retained the entered value and the detail page agreed. The reported one-day shift was not reproduced.

bugs.name: Milestone progress bar forces horizontal scrolling on mobile
bugs.summary: On a milestone detail page tall enough to scroll, at about 390px wide, the progress bar is reported to be a few pixels wider than the content area and to add a horizontal scrollbar.
bugs.expected: The reported expectation is that the milestone progress bar fits the mobile content width without horizontal scrolling.
bugs.actual: In a browser that draws a 15px classic scrollbar, a 390×844 window leaves 375px of content, and the progress bar (width min(420px, 96vw)) extends to about x=382, so the page scrolls sideways about 7px. With overlay scrollbars the bar fits.
reproSteps: Create a milestone with a long enough description that its detail page scrolls vertically.
Open the milestone detail page in a browser window about 390px wide.
Check whether the progress bar extends past the content edge and the page scrolls sideways.
bugs.reason: User-rejected. The overflow happens only when the browser draws a classic scrollbar that takes up width (96vw counts the scrollbar). Phone browsers and Mo's browser use overlay scrollbars, where the bar fits; Mo did not reproduce it at 390px. What remains is a desktop window dragged below about 437px wide, not a mobile bug.

bugs.name: Milestone description Preview renders bold Markdown as regular text
bugs.summary: The report claims that in the New Milestone form's description Preview, text written as **bold** loses its markers but shows at the same visible weight as the surrounding text.
bugs.expected: The reporter expects the bold words to look heavier than the surrounding text.
bugs.actual: At 390px, Preview of 'Normal text **Bold text** normal text' showed all three phrases at the same visible weight.
reproSteps: Open a repository's Milestones page and click New Milestone.
Enter 'Normal text **Bold text** normal text' in Description.
Click Preview and compare the bold phrase with the surrounding text.
bugs.reason: Not a Gitea defect. Preview returns Bold text and Gitea styles strong at weight 600 against 400 for paragraph text (web_src/css/base.css). The equal look comes from the browser's system-ui fallback font having only a regular face: a plain non-Gitea page shows the same thing, and forcing a font with a bold face makes the Gitea preview visibly bold. This matches the earlier bold rejections in releases, repository-code and wiki.

bugs.name: Closing a milestone from its details page leaves a blank page with no repository tabs
bugs.summary: The report claims that clicking Close on a milestone's details page navigates to a page where all repository tabs and body content disappear, leaving a blank white page below the top navigation bar. The rejected claim is that the page goes blank and the tabs disappear.
bugs.expected: The reporter expects the milestone list showing the closed milestone, or the milestone page with its updated status.
bugs.actual: After Close, the page was reported to show nothing below the top navigation bar.
reproSteps: Open a repository milestone's details page.
Click Close.
Observe the resulting page.
bugs.reason: Rejected claim: that the page goes blank and the repository tabs disappear. Both judges closed milestones from the details page at 1280px and 390px, and the repository header, tabs, search, Open/Closed toggle and New Milestone button always stayed visible; only the milestone list was empty. That empty list is a real bug, already labeled as gitea-milestone-close-redirects-to-state-close ('Closing a milestone opens an empty closed-milestone list') (the redirect uses state=close, which the page treats as Open), and is not what this entry rejects.

bugs.name: Saved milestone description renders bold Markdown as regular text
bugs.summary: The report claims that on a saved milestone's detail page, text written as **bold** in the description shows at the same visible weight as the surrounding text.
bugs.expected: The reporter expects the bold words to look heavier than the surrounding text.
bugs.actual: The milestone detail description displayed 'Normal text Bold text normal text' with uniform visible weight.
reproSteps: Create a milestone whose description contains 'Normal text **Bold text** normal text'.
Open the milestone's detail page and compare the bold phrase with the surrounding text.
bugs.reason: Not a Gitea defect. The description renders <strong> styled at weight 600 against 400 (web_src/css/base.css); the equal look comes from the browser's system-ui fallback font having only a regular face, as with the description Preview rejection and the earlier bold rejections in releases, repository-code and wiki.

bugs.name: Milestone detail page's Open tab lists closed issues
bugs.summary: The report says that on a milestone's detail page, clicking the "N Open" tab links to state=all and lists the milestone's closed issues alongside the open ones.
bugs.expected: The reporter expects clicking "N Open" to show only the milestone's open issues.
bugs.actual: On a milestone with two open issues and one closed issue, the default view had "2 Open" selected; its link was ?type=all&state=all&milestone=<id>, and clicking it listed all three issues, including the closed one.
reproSteps: Assign two open issues and one closed issue to a milestone.
Open the milestone's detail page with no state filter; "2 Open" is already selected.
Click "2 Open" and check the URL and the listed issues.
bugs.reason: Intended upstream behavior. The Open/Closed control in templates/repo/issue/openclose.tmpl is a toggle: clicking the already-selected Open filter deselects it and shows all states (go-gitea/gitea#28757, 'Add ability to see open and closed issues at the same time'). After choosing Closed, clicking Open goes to state=open and lists only open issues.

bugs.name: Organization Milestones team filter omits an all-repositories team
bugs.summary: The report claims the organization Milestones dashboard's Teams filter should list a team with All repositories access that the user joined, and Owners.
bugs.expected: The reporter expects the all-repositories team and Owners to be selectable in Filter by team repositories.
bugs.actual: The Teams menu offers All and a Specific-repositories team, but not the team with All repositories access or Owners, including after reload. Selecting the specific-repositories team scopes the milestones to its repository.
reproSteps: Create a disposable organization with two repositories and a milestone in each.
Create a team with All repositories access and a team with Specific repositories access to one repository; join both.
Open /org/<org>/milestones and expand Teams; only All and the specific-repositories team appear.
bugs.reason: Intended, with the same cause as the rejected organization Issues and Pull Requests team-filter reports (mo-12m-gitea-issues-8, gitea-pass2-008). The Milestones dashboard uses the shared user/dashboard/navbar template, which lists only teams without IncludesAllRepositories: filtering by an all-repositories team would equal All, so such teams, including Owners, are omitted. A Specific-repositories team appears and filters correctly.
